lines.japanese: 「はよー」
lines.english: “Morning.”

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 平日であれば三時間目の授業が始まるぐらいの時刻。
lines.english: On a weekday, it would have been about time for third period to begin.

lines.japanese: 僕と渡来さんは柳木原駅で待ちあわせた。
lines.english: Watarai and I met at Yanagihara Station.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、緊張してる」
lines.english: “You're nervous, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 質問ではなく断定だった。
lines.english: It was a statement, not a question.

lines.japanese: 「するよ、普通するって。むしろ渡来さん、なんでしないの」
lines.english: “Of course I am. Anybody would be. Why aren't you nervous?”

lines.japanese: 「んー？　全然してないこともないけど、そんな畏まることないんだって。うちの親、かなり大雑把なひとだから」
lines.english: “Hmm? It's not like I'm completely relaxed, but you don't have to be so formal about it. My mom's pretty easygoing.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ大雑把に別れてくださいとか言われたらどうしよう……」
lines.english: “What if she’s just as easygoing about telling us to break up...?”

lines.japanese: 「ないって、そういう後ろ向きの反応は。キホン放任主義で、昔から私の決断に反対したことなんてほとんどなかったし」
lines.english: “She won't. She doesn't react negatively like that. Her basic policy is to let me do what I want, and she's almost never opposed one of my decisions.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。でも、ほら……僕、ちょっと普通のひとと違うじゃない？　さすがに……」
lines.english: “I see. But... I'm a little different from an ordinary person, you know? Surely even she...”

lines.japanese: 「だーいじょぶ。渡来母、そんな細かいこと気にするようなタマじゃないから」
lines.english: “It'll be fiiine. Mama Watarai isn't the kind of woman who sweats little details like that.”

lines.japanese: 「細かいこと……かな」
lines.english: “Are they really... little details?”

lines.japanese: たしかに、いまはもう僕以外の僕が出ることもなく、お医者さんの話によれば「とりあえず安定している」とのことだ。
lines.english: It was true that none of my other selves had emerged lately, and according to my doctor, I was “stable for the time being.”

lines.japanese: しかし根治したわけではない。正直に言って、この先ぜったい何もないとは言いきれないのだ。
lines.english: But I wasn't cured. Honestly, no one could promise that nothing would ever happen again.

lines.japanese: 「そんなことより私の方が責められると思う」
lines.english: “If anything, I'm the one she's going to hassle.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、何度シミュレートしても、ニヤニヤ笑って冷やかしてくる以外の反応が考えられなくて。どーせ『告白のセリフはどんなの？』とか聞いてくんだよ」
lines.english: “No matter how many times I run the simulation, I can't imagine her doing anything but smirking and teasing me. She's definitely gonna ask, ‘So what did he say when he confessed?’”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そういう……愉快なお母さんなんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. She's that sort of... cheerful mother.”

lines.japanese: 僕は失礼にならない言葉を選んだ。今日ばかりは、天然だのＫＹだのと思われるわけにいかない。
lines.english: I chose a word that wouldn't sound rude. Today of all days, I couldn't let anyone think I was naturally clueless or unable to read a room.

lines.japanese: 「そう。イイひとはイイひとなんだけど、昔から愛情表現が厄介なの。娘いじりっていうか」
lines.english: “Yeah. She's a good person, but the way she shows affection has always been a pain. Like teasing her own daughter.”

lines.japanese: 「あんたはちょっと嫌がってるぐらいの顔がいちばん可愛い、とか幼い子供に真顔で言ってたし」
lines.english: “When I was a little kid, she'd look me dead in the eye and say, ‘You're cutest when you look a little uncomfortable.’”

lines.japanese: さすが親子だ。
lines.english: They truly were mother and daughter.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんの嗜虐趣味って、遺伝だったんだね」
lines.english: “So your sadistic streak is hereditary, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　誰が嗜虐趣味だって？　どの口が言った？」
lines.english: “Hm? Who has a sadistic streak? Did that just come out of your mouth?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あ、やめてよ渡来さん……足、足踏まないで……」
lines.english: “Ow, ow, stop, Watarai... My foot. Please stop stepping on my foot...”

lines.japanese: 「ほー？　羽田君ってさー、ちょっと嫌がってるぐらいの顔がいちばん可愛いくない？」
lines.english: “Oh? You know, Haneda, aren't you cutest when you look a little uncomfortable?”

lines.japanese: ほら、間違いない。
lines.english: There. No doubt about it.

lines.japanese: 受けつがれしＳの遺伝子。
lines.english: The inherited sadist gene.

lines.japanese: ふたり、黄色い線の内側で電車を待つ。
lines.english: The two of us waited behind the yellow line for the train.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは思案顔でうなっていた。
lines.english: Watarai groaned thoughtfully.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの」
lines.english: “What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「んー？　んー……」
lines.english: “Hmm? Hmmm...”

lines.japanese: 訊ねても回答はすぐに返ってこなかった。
lines.english: My question didn't receive an immediate answer.

lines.japanese: 「んっとねぇー……」
lines.english: “Well, you seeee...”

lines.japanese: 語尾を極端に長くひっぱった末に、彼女はのろのろと携帯電話を取りだした。
lines.english: After stretching the last syllable to an absurd length, she slowly took out her cell phone.

lines.japanese: 「……ちょっとこれ見て」
lines.english: “...Look at this.”

lines.japanese: すちゃっ。片手でケータイを開く。
lines.english: Snap. She opened the phone one-handed.

lines.japanese: しかし、見てと言ったわりに、渡来さんは画面をこちらへ向けてくれない。
lines.english: But despite telling me to look, Watarai didn't turn the screen my way.

lines.japanese: 僕は彼女の手元を覗きこむため、腰を曲げて首を伸ばした。
lines.english: I bent at the waist and craned my neck to peer down at her hand.

lines.japanese: なんだろう。金属的な色合いの幾何学模様。すでに何度か見せてもらったことのある、いつも通りの待ち受け画面だ。それとも、この中にどこか微細な変化でも──
lines.english: What was it? A metallic geometric pattern. It was the same wallpaper she had shown me several times before. Or had some minute detail somewhere in it changed—

lines.japanese: え？
lines.english: What?

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: まったくの不意打ちだった。一瞬──本当にわずか一瞬、彼女の唇が僕の頬に触れていった。
lines.english: It caught me completely off guard. For an instant—a truly tiny instant—her lips touched my cheek.

lines.japanese: 「な、なに……えっ？」
lines.english: “Wh-what... Huh?”

lines.japanese: 突然のキスに僕は動揺した。
lines.english: The sudden kiss flustered me.

lines.japanese: あまりに脈絡がなかったし、なにより格好つけたがりの渡来さんは、決して人前でそんなことをするひとじゃない。
lines.english: It had come with no warning at all. More importantly, Watarai liked to act cool and would never normally do such a thing in public.

lines.japanese: しかし彼女の答えは単純だった。
lines.english: But her answer was simple.

lines.japanese: 「今日はいちゃつけないから、いま一日分まとめた」
lines.english: “We won’t get to be all lovey-dovey today, so I gave you a whole day’s worth at once.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ……いい考えだね……」
lines.english: “Oh. Right... Good idea...”

lines.japanese: 我ながら間抜けな答えだ。
lines.english: What a foolish answer.

lines.japanese: それからしばらく僕は、右頬に残ったくすぐったい温度にのぼせて、格好悪いぐらいどぎまぎしていた。
lines.english: For some time afterward, the ticklish warmth lingering in my right cheek left me flushed and embarrassingly agitated.

lines.japanese: 電車の中で渡来さんは実家の話をいろいろしてくれたけど、半分ぐらいは耳に入ってこなかった。
lines.english: Watarai told me various things about her family on the train, but perhaps half of it never reached my ears.

lines.japanese: 「ねータカシ君さぁ、告白の台詞どんなんだったの？」
lines.english: “So, Takashi, what exactly did you say when you confessed?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、まあ……はは」
lines.english: “Oh, well, I... Haha.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんのお母さんは、事前情報どおりのひとだった。
lines.english: Watarai's mother was exactly as advertised.

lines.japanese: 「娘のことはぜんぶ任せるけど、結婚資金貯まるまで、避妊だけはしっかりね」
lines.english: “I'll leave my daughter entirely in your hands, but make sure you use protection until you've saved enough for the wedding.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、あの……はい」
lines.english: “Oh, um... Yes.”

lines.japanese: そして渡来さんのお母さんは、事前情報から予測していたよりも遥かにユニークなひとだった。
lines.english: And Watarai's mother was far more unique than even the advance warning had led me to expect.

lines.japanese: 「お母さん！　ちょっと、そういうお客さん相手みたいな冗談やめてよ」
lines.english: “Mom! Come on, quit joking with him like he’s one of your customers.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　何オカーサンって、気持ち悪い。あんたいつも、私のこと『ママ』って呼んでるじゃん」
lines.english: “Huh? What's with ‘Mom’? Creepy. You always call me ‘Mama.’”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そおだけどお！」
lines.english: “W-well, yeah, but!”

lines.japanese: あ、そうなんだ。
lines.english: Oh. She did.

lines.japanese: 「も、なんでいちいち彼氏の前でそおゆうこと言うかなあ！」
lines.english: “Why do you have to say every little thing in front of my boyfriend?”

lines.japanese: 「えー？　可愛いじゃない、大人になっても母親ママって呼ぶ女の子。ねえ？」
lines.english: “What? It's cute when a grown woman still calls her mother ‘Mama,’ isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい、そうですね」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. I think so.”

lines.japanese: 「あんた顔のわりに性格かわいくないんだから、そういうとこぐらいブリッとしてなきゃ、看板に偽りアリって訴えられちゃうからね」
lines.english: “With that face and your not-so-cute personality, you have to act girly somewhere or somebody'll sue you for false advertising.”

lines.japanese: 「いいの。余計なお世話」
lines.english: “I don't care. Mind your own business.”

lines.japanese: 「ねーねー？　タカシ君って、いま何人の子と付きあってんの？」
lines.english: “Hey, Takashi. How many girls are you dating?”

lines.japanese: 「は……ハっ？　いままで、ですか」
lines.english: “How... many? You mean in my life?”

lines.japanese: 「ちーがうよ、過去なんてどーでもいい。いまナウ現在」
lines.english: “Nooo. Who cares about the past? I mean now. Right now. Currently.”

lines.japanese: 「現在！？　い、いえ、わた……明日香さん、だけです、もちろん」
lines.english: “Currently?! N-no, Wata... Asuka is the only one. Of course.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ～？　あいつには黙っとくから、ホントのこと教えてよ～」
lines.english: “Reeeally? I won't tell her, so give me the truth.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、活きのイイ子いたらオバさんに貸してくれない？　ひとりでいいから。うちの店、いま若いバイト探してんだよねー」
lines.english: “Oh, and if you know any lively girls, could you lend me one? Just one. My shop needs a young part-timer.”

lines.japanese: 「活きのイイ、ですか……えっと、じゃあ付きあってはいないけど、高内さんにでも聞いてみようかな……」
lines.english: “A lively girl... Well, I'm not dating her, but perhaps I could ask Takauchi...”

lines.japanese: 「はいはいマジレスしない。そんなんほっときゃいいから」
lines.english: “Yes, yes, don't answer that seriously. Just ignore her.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんのお母さんは、いろいろな意味で渡来さんのお母さんだった。
lines.english: In a great many ways, Watarai's mother was unmistakably Watarai's mother.

lines.japanese: このひとと共に暮らして、このひとから影響を受けたり、支えあったりしながらいまの渡来明日香という素敵な女の子が形作られたのだと思うと、なんだかとても感慨深い。
lines.english: When I imagined that Asuka Watarai, the wonderful girl I knew, had taken shape while living with this woman, influenced by her and supporting each other, I felt deeply moved.

lines.japanese: 親子っていいな。そう思った。
lines.english: Parents and children were wonderful. That was what I thought.
“Phew...”

lines.japanese: お母さんは煙草に火を点け、頬杖をついた。
lines.english: Her mother lit a cigarette and rested her cheek on one hand.

lines.japanese: 「まっ、明日香はあんなんでも私の娘だから、オトコ見る目だけはあるでしょ」
lines.english: “Well, whatever else you can say about Asuka, she is my daughter. At least she knows how to pick a man.”

lines.japanese: 「だけって」
lines.english: “At least?”

lines.japanese: まるで友達同士みたいな空気。いつか本当に、僕もこの中に加われる日が来たらいいと思う。
lines.english: The air between them was almost like two friends. I hoped the day would come when I could truly join them.

lines.japanese: 「ねえタカシ君。私、生きてく分稼ぐのに必死で、この子には寂しい思いさせちゃった時期もあってね」
lines.english: “Listen, Takashi. I was so busy scraping together enough for us to live that there was a time when I left this girl lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい」
lines.english: “Y-yes.”

lines.japanese: 「なーんか捻くれちゃったトコもあるけど、でも間違った人間にだけは育ててないから」
lines.english: “Some parts of her came out a little twisted, but I never raised her to be wrong where it counts.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと……オカン、ひょっとして飲んでんの？」
lines.english: “Wait... Ma, have you been drinking?”

lines.japanese: 「飲むでしょ、そりゃ。娘が初めて彼氏連れてくるめでたい日なんだもん」
lines.english: “Of course I'm drinking. My daughter brought her first boyfriend home. It's a day to celebrate.”

lines.japanese: 「もぉー、なにそれ。終わってからにしてよ」
lines.english: “Come on. What is this? At least wait until afterward.”

lines.japanese: 「いいの、いいの。そういう日もある」
lines.english: “It's fine, it's fine. Some days are like that.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは」
lines.english: “Ahaha.”

lines.japanese: うん、親子だなあ。
lines.english: Yes. They were mother and daughter.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、タカシ君。さっき説明してくれた病気の話だけど」
lines.english: “Oh, Takashi. About the condition you explained earlier.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんのお母さんは、あたかも空気の変容を妨げるかのように、ゆったりした楽な姿勢を崩さなかった。
lines.english: As if she refused to let the atmosphere change, Watarai's mother remained in the same easy, relaxed posture.

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: しかし僕は、背筋を伸ばして居住まいを正した。
lines.english: But I straightened my back and composed myself.

lines.japanese: 「私１６ンときにはもう働いててガッコー行ってないからさ、小難しいこと言われてもよく分かンないんだよね」
lines.english: “I was already working by sixteen and didn't go to school anymore, so I don't really follow all the complicated stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、あの子が選んだオトコなら間違いはないって、信じるから。いいでしょ？　ぜったい泣かせないよね？」
lines.english: “But I trust that a man my daughter chose can't be wrong. All right? You'll never make her cry, will you?”

lines.japanese: 喉が絡んでしまないよう一度咳払いをしてから、僕はお母さんの瞳を見据えて堂々と答えた。
lines.english: I cleared my throat once so my voice wouldn't catch, then met her mother's eyes and answered firmly.

lines.japanese: 「はい。もちろ」
lines.english: “Yes. Of cour—”

lines.japanese: 「なんちゃってー！」
lines.english: “Just kidding!”

lines.japanese: 答えたかったけど、最後までは言わせてもらえなかった。
lines.english: I wanted to answer, but she didn't let me finish.

lines.japanese: このひとは、どこまでも渡来さんのお母さんだった。
lines.english: This woman was Watarai's mother through and through.

lines.japanese: 「あーあ、なんだこの茶番」
lines.english: “God, what a farce.”

lines.japanese: 僕の隣りで、大袈裟に音をあげて席を立つひとがいた。
lines.english: The person beside me stood with an exaggerated groan.

lines.japanese: 「ママ、お昼まだでしょ。なんか軽く作ったげる」
lines.english: “Mama, you haven't eaten lunch yet, right? I'll make you something light.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがキッチンへ消えて、お母さんが土曜の昼番組を点ける。ほっとする穏やかな生活音。
lines.english: Watarai disappeared into the kitchen, and her mother turned on a Saturday afternoon show. The soothing sounds of an ordinary life filled the room.

lines.japanese: 僕はちょっと襟元を緩めて、大きく息を吐いた。
lines.english: I loosened my collar a little and let out a long breath.

lines.japanese: 適度に緊張が融けてゆく。三人で囲む昼餉がわりと楽しみだった。
lines.english: The tension gradually eased away. I found myself rather looking forward to the three of us sharing lunch.

lines.japanese: 「ママー、お茶漬けでいいよねー」
lines.english: “Mama, tea over rice is fine, right?”

lines.japanese: 「パスタぁー」
lines.english: “Pastaaa.”

lines.japanese: 「シャケと梅どっちがいー？」
lines.english: “Salmon or plum?”

lines.japanese: 「ウニイカ明太ー」
lines.english: “Sea urchin, squid, and spicy cod roe.”
